body.statement: On the fixed horizon \(T=5\), the construction \(\mathfrak W_{2/185}\) consists of two strictly positive stochastic three-state realizations with \(p_0>0\), full predictive rank, and invertible killed dynamics. The two realizations generate exactly the same probabilities for every stopped word observable on dates \(0,\ldots,5\) and the same post-adoption outcomes. At the fixed cohort \(g=0\), \(\mu^0_{0,0}=46/95\) in both realizations, whereas \(\mu^0_{0,1}=457/950\) and \((\mu^0_{0,1})'=17289/35150\), so \((\mu^0_{0,1})'-\mu^0_{0,1}=2/185\). With their common constant treated outcome, \((\tau_{0,1})'-\tau_{0,1}=-2/185\).
body.justification: The exact pair is a stress test for transported fitted-latent-state workflows and observed-history matching under unmodeled evolving hidden selection.
body.gap: All stopped-panel observables agree while the fixed \(T=5\), \(g=0\), \(r=1\) ATT coordinate differs. This necessitates an extra restriction but does not contradict Pennoni, Paas, and Bartolucci, Clouth, Bijlsma, Pauws, and Vermunt, Kim and Lee, or Ishimaru because their identifying conditions are not asserted on this pair.
body.consumer: The rational pair is a reproducible stress test: any transported latent-state fit or Kim--Lee-style observed-history match must expose which extra restriction selects one of its two \(\tau_{0,1}\) values.
